Semester 5: Child, Mental Health & Community

Read the summary line. If it feels unfamiliar, open the chapter and study the diagram.

Child Health Nursing I

Introduction to Child Health Nursing

  • Child health nursing in India — why children are different, the national child health programme and the nurse’s role.
  • Define the scope of child health nursing
  • Explain why children are not small adults

Community Health Nursing I

Concepts of Community Health Nursing

  • Community health nursing concepts — community, health, primary health care, levels of prevention and the nurse’s role.
  • Define community and community health
  • Describe primary health care and its elements

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Foundations of Education

  • Education in nursing — philosophy, aims, the nurse educator’s role, and the nursing curriculum.
  • Describe the meaning and aims of education
  • Explain the nursing curriculum

Forensic Nursing & Indian Laws

Forensic Science & Violence

  • Forensic science basics — medico-legal cases, types of injuries, violence and the nurse’s role in evidence and victim care.
  • Define forensic science and its branches
  • Describe types of injuries and their medico-legal importance

Mental Health Nursing I

Introduction to Mental Health Nursing

  • What mental health is, what mental illness is, the historical background and the scope of mental health nursing.
  • Define mental health and mental illness
  • List the signs of positive mental health

Child Health Nursing I

The Healthy Child: Growth & Development

  • Growth and development in infants and children — principles, milestones, and nursing assessment.
  • Define growth and development
  • Describe principles of growth and development

Community Health Nursing I

Health Planning & Delivery System

  • Health planning, the Indian health care delivery system and the levels, infrastructure and referral chain.
  • Describe the steps of health planning
  • Explain the levels of health care delivery in India

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Assessment, Curriculum & Planning

  • Writing objectives, planning lessons and assessing learner needs — the foundations of teaching design.
  • Write behavioural objectives in the three domains
  • Plan a lesson with the standard components

Forensic Nursing & Indian Laws

Forensic Nursing

  • Forensic nursing — definition, role of the nurse in evidence, death certification and care of the dying and the dead.
  • Define forensic nursing
  • Describe the roles of a forensic nurse

Mental Health Nursing I

Principles & Concepts of Mental Health Nursing

  • Core concepts — mind, personality, defence mechanisms, stress, models of mental illness, classification and nursing principles.
  • Describe the structure of the mind: id, ego and superego
  • List common defence mechanisms

Child Health Nursing I

Care of the Neonate (ENBC)

  • Essential newborn care — immediate assessment at birth, warmth, cord care, feeding, vitamin K and danger signs.
  • Describe the steps of essential newborn care
  • Assess a newborn using the Apgar score

Community Health Nursing I

Environmental Health & Sanitation

  • Environmental health — water, sanitation, waste, ventilation, vectors, housing and pollution, with the nurse’s role.
  • Explain safe and sufficient water supply
  • Describe excreta and refuse disposal

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Classroom & Skill-Lab Teaching

  • Classroom teaching methods, micro-teaching, and skill laboratory practice in nursing education.
  • Use classroom teaching methods appropriately
  • Describe micro-teaching

Forensic Nursing & Indian Laws

Forensic Team & Evidence Preservation

  • The forensic team, evidence types and preservation, and nursing responsibilities in medico-legal investigation.
  • List the members of the forensic team
  • Describe evidence types and preservation

Mental Health Nursing I

Mental Health Assessment

  • Assessing a psychiatric patient — history, mental status examination, risk assessment and the standard rating scales.
  • Take a psychiatric history in order
  • Perform a mental status examination

Child Health Nursing I

Integrated Management of Childhood Illness

  • IMNCI — the WHO approach to sick children: assess and classify danger signs, then treat by colour-coded plans.
  • Describe the IMNCI process
  • List general danger signs in a child

Community Health Nursing I

Nutrition Assessment & Education

  • Community nutrition assessment — surveys, anthropometry, deficiency detection and nutrition education.
  • Describe methods of community nutrition assessment
  • Use anthropometry and growth monitoring

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Clinical Teaching

  • Clinical teaching in nursing wards — methods, preparation of students, patient assignment and clinical evaluation.
  • Describe clinical teaching methods
  • Explain preparation for a clinical posting

Forensic Nursing & Indian Laws

Indian Constitution & Rights

  • The Indian Constitution, patient rights and duties, and legal rights relevant to nursing practice.
  • Describe the Preamble, fundamental rights and duties
  • List the rights of the patient

Mental Health Nursing I

Therapeutic Communication & Relationship

  • Building the nurse-patient relationship — phases, techniques, blocks and therapeutic communication skills.
  • Describe the phases of the nurse-patient relationship
  • Use therapeutic communication techniques

Child Health Nursing I

Common Childhood Diseases

  • Common childhood illness — diarrhoea, pneumonia, measles, malnutrition, anaemia, worm infestation and their nursing care.
  • Describe the causes and prevention of diarrhoea
  • Explain the nursing care of pneumonia

Community Health Nursing I

Communication & Health Education

  • Health communication and health education — methods, media, the teaching process and evaluation.
  • Describe elements of communication
  • Plan health education for a group

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Teaching Media & Technology

  • Teaching media and technology — projected aids, video, computers, e-learning and telehealth for nursing education.
  • Select teaching media appropriate to learners
  • Describe projected and non-projected aids

Forensic Nursing & Indian Laws

Indian Judicial System & Laws

  • The Indian judicial system, courts, criminal law and key statutes affecting nursing practice and patient care.
  • Describe the Indian judicial system
  • Differentiate criminal and civil law

Mental Health Nursing I

Treatment Modalities & Therapies

  • Psychiatric treatment — pharmacological therapy, ECT, psychotherapy and psychosocial rehabilitation.
  • Describe the roles of psychiatric medicines
  • Explain the procedure and nursing care in ECT

Child Health Nursing I

Childhood Emergencies & PLS

  • Childhood emergencies and Paediatric Life Support — recognition, choking, convulsions, shock, burns and the ABCDE approach.
  • Recognise a child in cardiorespiratory distress
  • Demonstrate the choking algorithm for infants and children

Community Health Nursing I

Community Health Nursing Approaches & Home Visits

  • Community nursing approaches — home visits, surveys, school and industry health, and working with volunteers.
  • Describe the purpose and process of a home visit
  • Explain community surveys and records

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Assessment & Evaluation

  • Assessment and evaluation in nursing education — tools, blueprints, attendance, clinical records and university examinations.
  • Differentiate measurement, assessment, evaluation
  • Describe tools of assessment

Mental Health Nursing I

Schizophrenia & Psychotic Disorders

  • Schizophrenia — symptoms, types, causes, treatment and the nursing care of psychotic patients.
  • Describe the symptoms of schizophrenia
  • List the types of schizophrenia

Community Health Nursing I

Family Health Nursing

  • The family as the unit of care — family assessment, family life cycle, roles and family health nursing process.
  • Describe the family as a unit of care
  • List the stages of the family life cycle

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Guidance & Counselling

  • Guidance and counselling in nursing — types of guidance, counselling skills and the nurse as counselor.
  • Differentiate guidance and counselling
  • List types of guidance

Mental Health Nursing I

Mood Disorders

  • Mood disorders — depressive illness, mania, bipolar disorder, suicide risk and nursing care.
  • Describe the symptoms of depression and mania
  • Differentiate depression from normal sadness

Community Health Nursing I

Epidemiology

  • Epidemiology — health and disease in populations, the epidemiology chain, disease prevention, surveillance and investigation of outbreaks.
  • Define epidemiology and its uses
  • Describe the chain of infection and ways to break it

Educational Technology / Nursing Education

Ethics & Evidence-Based Teaching

  • Ethics in nursing education and evidence-based teaching — honest assessment, fair practice and using research to teach better.
  • Apply ethical principles in teaching and assessment
  • Address malpractice and misconduct

Mental Health Nursing I

Neurotic, Stress & Somatoform Disorders

  • Anxiety, phobia, panic, OCD, PTSD, conversion and somatisation — recognition and nursing care.
  • Describe anxiety disorders and their management
  • Differentiate phobia, panic and generalised anxiety

Community Health Nursing I

National Health Programmes

  • Major national programmes — TB, HIV, malaria, RCH, universal immunisation, leprosy, blindness, nutrition and NCD
  • Describe the national programmes of relevance to nursing
  • Explain the nurse’s role in TB, HIV and malaria control

Community Health Nursing I

Occupational, Geriatric & Mental Health

  • Community care of special groups — workers, older adults and people with mental illness.
  • Describe occupational health care in the community
  • Describe care of the elderly
